questions.text: What does PostgreSQL logical replication transfer?

answers.text: Changes to rows in selected tables
A byte-for-byte copy of the entire cluster
Only the text of executed SQL commands
Only system catalog files

questions.explanation: Logical replication transfers table row changes, not a physical copy of files and not the original SQL command text.

questions.text: Which properties of logical replication distinguish it from physical replication? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Individual tables can be replicated selectively
Binary compatibility between servers is not required
The data flow can be organized in different directions
It always creates an exact copy of the entire cluster

questions.explanation: Logical replication operates at a higher level: it allows selecting tables, does not require binary compatibility, and can be used in multidirectional topologies.

source.locator: Comparison of physical and logical replication

questions.text: Which model is used by PostgreSQL built-in logical replication?

answers.text: Publication — subscription
Shared disk array
Two-phase commit across all servers
Periodic pg_dump — pg_restore

questions.explanation: A publication is defined on the publishing server, while another server creates a subscription and receives the corresponding changes.

questions.text: What can a publication define in PostgreSQL 16? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The set of published tables
The set of published columns
A row filter condition
The physical directory where table files are stored on the subscriber

questions.explanation: A publication defines a logical data set. The material specifically notes that only selected columns and rows of a table can be published.

questions.text: What does the logical replication worker do on the subscriber server?

answers.text: Receives changes and applies them on the subscriber
Creates a physical backup of the publishing server
Runs CHECKPOINT on the publishing server
Compiles received SQL code before sending it to the publisher

questions.explanation: In the course diagram, the wal sender is on the source side, while the logical replication worker on the subscriber receives and applies changes.

source.locator: wal sender and logical replication worker

questions.text: Which statements about data transfer between a publication and a subscription are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Row changes are replicated, not the original SQL commands
The subscriber applies the received changes without normal parsing and planning of the original SQL command
A logical replication slot is used for transfer
The subscriber must re-execute the original query text from the publisher

questions.explanation: Logical replication transfers the result of data changes at row level. The subscriber does not need to execute the publisher's original SQL command again.

questions.text: What can happen when a subscription is created for tables that already contain data?

answers.text: An initial synchronization of table contents can be performed
The schema of all tables is always created automatically from the publication DDL
The entire subscriber cluster is replaced with a physical copy of the publisher
All local subscriber data is always deleted

questions.explanation: Initial data synchronization can be performed when a subscription is created, but the required tables must already exist on the subscriber.

questions.text: Which statements about initial synchronization and table structure are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Table contents can be copied during initial synchronization
Publication DDL commands are not transferred automatically
Target tables on the subscriber must be prepared in advance
CREATE TABLE on the publisher automatically creates the same table on every subscriber

questions.explanation: Logical replication synchronizes data but does not transfer schema automatically. DDL must be applied separately.

questions.text: Why is replica identity required for UPDATE and DELETE in logical replication?

answers.text: To identify the old version of the row being updated or deleted
To select the directory for WAL files
To determine the user who executed the query
To encrypt the connection between servers

questions.explanation: INSERT creates a new row, while for UPDATE and DELETE the subscriber must determine which existing row should be changed or removed.

questions.text: Which row identification methods does PostgreSQL logical replication support? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Primary key columns
A suitable unique index
All columns of the row
Only the physical block number and row offset

questions.explanation: The primary key is used by default, but REPLICA IDENTITY can select a suitable unique index or use all columns.

questions.text: How does logical replication handle DDL commands?

answers.text: DDL is not replicated automatically; schema changes must be transferred separately
DDL is always executed automatically on all subscribers
DDL is replicated only for views
DDL is first converted into a physical WAL clone of the entire cluster

questions.explanation: One of the main limitations of built-in logical replication is that schema changes are not transferred automatically.

questions.text: What is not replicated by built-in logical replication? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: DDL commands
Sequence values
Large objects (lo)
Row changes in ordinary published tables

questions.explanation: The course specifically lists DDL, sequence values, and large objects as data that standard logical replication does not transfer.

questions.text: Which relations can directly participate in built-in logical replication?

answers.text: Regular base tables and partitioned tables
Only regular views
Only materialized views
Only foreign tables

questions.explanation: The material limits direct logical replication to regular base tables and partitioned tables; views and foreign tables are not included.

questions.text: Which problems can occur because sequence values are not replicated? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Two servers can attempt to use the same surrogate key value
A uniqueness constraint violation can occur
Different identifier ranges can be assigned to servers to reduce the risk
PostgreSQL automatically synchronizes a sequence after every INSERT

questions.explanation: If writes are possible on multiple servers, independent sequences can generate overlapping values. The course suggests separate ranges or UUIDs.

questions.text: What happens if applying a logically replicated change violates an integrity constraint on the subscriber?

answers.text: Applying changes is paused until the conflict is resolved manually
The subscriber automatically deletes the conflicting row
The publishing server automatically rolls back the original transaction
The conflict is ignored without a message

questions.explanation: There is no universal automatic resolution for such conflicts. The apply process stops until an administrator fixes the cause.

questions.text: Which statements about logical replication conflicts are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A conflict can involve local data on the subscriber
An integrity constraint violation can cause a conflict
Universal automatic conflict resolution is not supported
Every conflict is automatically resolved using last-write-wins

questions.explanation: The subscriber remains a regular PostgreSQL database and can contain its own data, so applying incoming changes can conflict with that data.

questions.text: Why is the subscription parameter streaming useful for long-running transactions?

answers.text: It allows changes to be sent to the subscriber before a long transaction commits, reducing the need to retain them only on the publisher side
It automatically converts logical replication into physical replication
It prevents long-running transactions from executing
It sends only DDL commands to the subscriber

questions.explanation: The material notes the issue with long-running transactions and the ability of streaming to send changes earlier, storing or applying them on the subscriber side.

questions.text: Which tasks can PostgreSQL logical replication solve? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Consolidating data from multiple branches
Transferring changes in both directions between servers
Moving between PostgreSQL major versions while reducing service interruption
Byte-for-byte mirroring of the entire PostgreSQL file system

questions.explanation: The course presents logical replication as a more flexible mechanism for selective data consolidation, multidirectional topologies, and migration between versions.

questions.text: Why can logical replication be used when moving between different PostgreSQL major versions?

answers.text: It does not require binary compatibility between servers; protocol compatibility is sufficient
It copies executables from the old version to the new server
It forces the new server to use the old version's file format
It automatically upgrades all extensions and DDL without preparation

questions.explanation: Physical replication depends on binary compatibility, while logical replication transfers changes through a logical protocol, making migration between major versions possible.

questions.text: What must be considered when building bidirectional logical replication for the same table between two servers? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Data can be changed locally on both servers
The possibility of conflicts must be considered
The uniqueness of generated identifiers must be planned
Built-in logical replication automatically resolves any concurrent changes

questions.explanation: A bidirectional topology is possible, but both servers remain active and can modify data. Therefore, constraints, sequences, and conflicts become a design and administration responsibility.

questions.text: Which wal_level value is required on the publishing server for built-in logical replication?

answers.text: logical
minimal
replica without additional logical decoding information
off

questions.explanation: Logical decoding requires wal_level = logical, which adds the information needed to interpret row changes.

questions.text: What consequences can a logical replication slot that remains inactive for a long time have? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The publisher must retain WAL still needed by the subscriber
The cleanup horizon can be held back
Disk space consumption on the publisher can grow
An inactive slot automatically switches the subscriber to physical replication

questions.explanation: The slot preserves data required by a lagging subscriber; prolonged inactivity requires monitoring WAL retention and cleanup.

questions.text: What is important when replicating TRUNCATE for tables related by foreign keys?

answers.text: The required related tables must be present in the subscription; otherwise applying TRUNCATE can fail
TRUNCATE always ignores foreign keys on the subscriber
TRUNCATE is automatically converted into DELETE for every row
For TRUNCATE, it is sufficient to include only the sequence associated with the table

questions.explanation: Logical replication restrictions require foreign keys to be considered: applying TRUNCATE must be valid on the subscriber side.

questions.text: How should a logical subscription to a publication in the same cluster be created to avoid blocking during slot creation? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Create the logical replication slot separately
Specify create_slot = false in CREATE SUBSCRIPTION
Avoid having the same command wait for slot creation through its own connection
A physical slot must be used instead of a logical one

questions.explanation: In PostgreSQL 16, CREATE SUBSCRIPTION within the same cluster can hang if it also tries to create the slot; the documentation recommends creating the logical slot separately and using create_slot = false.

questions.text: Which subscription parameters help configure bidirectional logical replication without recopying existing data or sending already received changes back to the source? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: copy_data = false — do not repeat the initial copy of existing rows
origin = none — request changes without a replication origin and reduce the risk of sending already received changes back
Both parameters are specified when creating subscriptions on the two servers in the exercise
origin = any guarantees automatic resolution of master-master conflicts

questions.explanation: The practical bidirectional topology in the course explicitly uses copy_data = false and origin = none; conflicts must still be prevented by design.
